text:
incident-bot: ALERT: kv-cache cont-batch spike detected in prod (region us-west-2). metric: kv_active_entries +1200% in 3m, tail latency ↑ 3x. tagging models: mistral-v2*, qwen-13B-mqa. paging oncall: @Ben (oncall). Severity: P1 — possible customer impact.

Ben (oncall): seeing alerts, joining. any ETA on root cause?

Carol (sre): early signal looks like prefetch + continuous-batching combinatoric blowup. lots of small prefixes causing kv hotspotting and batch fanout.

Dave (runtime): confirmed. KV shards hitting eviction + GC thrash. continuous_batcher queues exploded — we see 200ms -> 900ms token latencies for MQA routes.

Alice (mlops): models implicated: qwen-mqa and a mistral variant with high prefix overlap from an experiment. GQA routes less affected but noisy.

Erin (support): we already have a customer (acct: acme-inc) reporting slow responses since ~09:12 UTC, rate 5% errors 502. They asked if we're aware.

Victor (solutions): notifying enterprise contacts for acme-inc, sending preliminary note. keep me posted on mitigation.

Ben (oncall): immediate plan: 1) throttle continuous batching for MQA routes 2) disable prefetch/prefix caching for suspected model groups 3) scale kv replicas if needed. who can push hotfix?

Dave (runtime): I can cut a config hotfix to disable continuous batching for the affected service pool. prepping patch now. placing a canary to 5% first.

deploy-bot: deploy triggered by Dave: hotfix/kv-contbatch-throttle -> staging -> canary (5%). CI: green.

Carol (sre): add monitoring alert to watch kv_eviction_rate, contbatch_queue_length, tail_latency_95. also set pager mute to avoid noise.

Dave (runtime): hotfix config snippet (will apply to service pool 'inference-mqa-usw2'):

```yaml
continuous_batching:
  enabled: false  # temporary, disables cross-request batching for this pool
  max_batch_size: 1
  batch_window_ms: 0
prefetch:
  enabled: false
  prefix_cache_size: 0
```

Ben (oncall): applying now to canary. switching 5% traffic.

deploy-bot: canary live -> 5% traffic. health checks running.

Carol (sre): initial canary metrics: kv_active_entries down 45% in canary, tail latency down ~60% vs affected baseline. no increase in error rates.

Alice (mlops): good sign. disabling prefetch should stop the combinatorial insertion pattern. But we need longer run to ensure eviction cascade won't hit other pools.

Ben (oncall): warming up for wider deploy. if canary holds for 10m, move to 50% then 100%.

Erin (support): sending update to acme-inc: "We're aware of increased latency; engineering applied a mitigation and we'll follow up with details once stabilized."

Victor (solutions): also told them we may have to throttle some experimental routes; they said ok to prioritize stability.

Dave (runtime): promoting to 50%.

deploy-bot: canary -> 50% traffic. health checks OK.

Carol (sre): metrics at 50%: cluster-wide kv_eviction_rate trending down, overall 95p latency trending down ~40% from peak. some noise on unrelated llama routes but within SLO.

Ben (oncall): continue to 100%. keep rollback plan ready.

Dave (runtime): promoting to 100% now.

deploy-bot: deployment complete: hotfix/kv-contbatch-throttle -> 100%.

Carol (sre): incident-bot: update status -> mitigation applied. monitoring will now watch for regressions.

Ben (oncall): immediate customer impact reduced. acme-inc reports improved responses. marking P1 -> P2 for monitoring.

Alice (mlops): follow-up: we need a targeted fix rather than broad disable. plan: 1) identify offending experiment that increased prefix overlap 2) add heuristic to continuous_batcher to avoid cross-request merging when prefix cardinality high 3) re-enable prefetch with bounds.

Dave (runtime): I'll open an RFC for the batching heuristic. Also will add a circuit-breaker to prefetch that trips if eviction_rate > threshold.

Erin (support): drafting post-incident message for customers: timeline + mitigations + workaround (disable experimental routing on their side if they used it).

Victor (solutions): coordinated with acme-inc to run a small traffic replay to validate stability; they agreed to a 1h window tomorrow.

Ben (oncall): postmortem owners: Carol (ops lead), Dave (runtime), Alice (mlops). action items assigned. I'll hand off to follow-up rotation in 4h.

Carol (sre): quick root cause hypothesis: prefetch + continuous batcher combined with a rollout of an A/B experiment on MQA routes created high prefix-cardinality write amplification into KV layer causing eviction thrash and GC pauses.

Ben (oncall): any customer-facing credit action? finance/CS to advise.

Erin (support): will loop in CS.

Dave (runtime): next steps immediate: reintroduce soft-limits on batch fanout, add telemetry for prefix-cardinality per route, and backfill the hot paths in docs.

Carol (sre): final note: resolved for now, watch period 6h. if tail latency climbs again, we revert and open full incident.

Ben (oncall): thanks all. I’m off for handoff in 4h — will drop a handoff message in #oncall-handoff.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED -> mitigation applied; severity downgraded to P2; monitoring watch window started.

Erin (support): posting customer follow-up now.

Victor (solutions): filing a customer-facing summary after we agree on final RCA draft.

Carol (sre): adding pointers for long-term: batching heuristics RFC, prefetch circuit-breaker, model rollout guard rails.

Ben (oncall): logging done. handing off. good job team. :thumbsup:
